correctness.rationale: Conditioning on thermal Brownian noise reduces C(t) to Gaussian expectation exp(−2I_s−J_t). Direct integrated OU covariances yield C(t)=2Dx exp[−λt−d(1−e^(−µt))] Iµ(A,2d(1+e^(−µt))), with d=Dk/µ³, A=2κ−4Dk/µ²>0, λ=κ−Dk/µ². The averaged impulse G uses only J_t, so C/(C0G)=Iµ(A,2d(1+e^(−µt)))/Iµ(A,4d)>1 and increases. Tilt derivative ∂A M=−Cov(S,h)<0 and ∂bM=−Var(h)<0, h=1−e^(−µS), establishes two unique ordered M=1/2 thresholds and envelope derivative dµe^(−µt)(2M−1), hence no maxima and one strict minimum exactly in middle regime. Independent quadrature found a_-<a_+ at d=0.04, 0.2, 1; full proof is analytic. Taylor of bounded tilted expectation controls t→∞ and d→0 boundary.
residual_risks: Strict finite-variance parameter A>0 and independent noises essential; only rescaled envelope can have minimum.
